[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_alloydb_user.users` references the cluster but not the primary instance. AlloyDB user creation requires the primary instance to be created first; the provider documentation's user examples explicitly depend on the instance.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The AlloyDB user resource should wait for the primary instance to be created before creating database users. The provider's documented user examples explicitly depend on the instance; depending only on the cluster does not ensure the instance is ready.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_alloydb_user.users only references google_alloydb_cluster.primary (cluster = google_alloydb_cluster.primary.id), and google_alloydb_instance.primary depends on that same cluster, so users and the primary instance are unordered siblings. A google_alloydb_user can only be created once the cluster has a running primary instance (the provider's own examples for this resource always set depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.<primary>]), so creating the users can race instance provisioning and fail with the cluster not yet able to accept users. Add depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary] to the users resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
google_alloydb_user.users has no dependency on google_alloydb_instance.primary; its only ordering dependency is the primary cluster (cluster = google_alloydb_cluster.primary.id). AlloyDB only allows database users/roles to be created once the cluster has a primary instance — the provider's documented examples for both ALLOYDB_BUILT_IN and ALLOYDB_IAM_USER users explicitly add `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.<primary>]`. Without it, applying a fresh project can race: Terraform may attempt users.create while the primary instance is still provisioning, and the API call fails. Add `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary]` to google_alloydb_user.users.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_alloydb_user.users only depends on google_alloydb_cluster.primary (its `cluster` argument), so Terraform can create the database users before the cluster has any primary instance. The AlloyDB users API requires the cluster's primary instance to exist/be ready first — the google_alloydb_user provider documentation adds `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.default]` to both the ALLOYDB_BUILT_IN and ALLOYDB_IAM_USER examples for exactly this reason. Without an ordering edge to google_alloydb_instance.primary, `terraform apply` on a fresh project can fail (or force a re-apply) when creating users. Add `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary]` to google_alloydb_user.users.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_alloydb_user.users is provisioned on google_alloydb_cluster.primary without any ordering guarantee relative to google_alloydb_instance.primary. Per the provider documentation, database users should only be created after the primary instance exists (the official examples attach depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.default] to google_alloydb_user), since user provisioning requires the instance backing the cluster to be in place. Add a bare `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary]` to google_alloydb_user.users.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`google_alloydb_user.users` only depends on `google_alloydb_cluster.primary` (via its `cluster` attribute). Creating database users is a real-world operation that requires the cluster's primary instance to exist first — the official provider documentation for google_alloydb_user includes `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance...]` in every example. Without this ordering, Terraform may create the users concurrently with (or before) `google_alloydb_instance.primary`, and user creation can fail or race against instance provisioning. Add an explicit `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary]`; there is no attribute on the user resource that can reference the instance, so a data-dependency fix is not applicable.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_alloydb_user.users only depends on google_alloydb_cluster.primary (via the cluster attribute), but creating database users in an AlloyDB cluster requires the cluster's primary instance to exist and be ready first. The provider documentation's own google_alloydb_user examples include depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.default] for this reason. Without this ordering, user creation can race ahead of instance provisioning and fail.
